title: [R-30] Give the payment-method advisory-lock identity one owner
description:
Audit ID: R-30
Authoritative subsystem: PG-05
Final rank: 1 of 32
Disposition: recommend
Impact: critical privacy/concurrency
Confidence: high
Estimated effort: medium + operational
Blast radius: high

## Evidence
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/deletion.rs:101
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/deletion.rs:125
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/deletion.rs:397
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/deletion.rs:634
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/enrollment_application.rs:910
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/src/enrollment_application/initial/approval.rs:36
- crates/syrup-rail-postgres/AGENTS.md:309

## Current Complexity
Deletion and payment writers claim the same mutation domain but hash different strings; their advisory locks never contend, and deletion's test repeats its own wrong key. Approval can race scrubbing and potentially restore mutable data.

## Proposed Representation
One neutral crate-private typed payment-method-domain lock helper used by writers and deletion, preserving the established writer key gateway_account_id:subscriber_id.

## Smallest Credible Scope
deletion.rs/tests, enrollment_application.rs helper visibility or new private lock module/lib declaration; public commands unchanged.

## Regression Risk and Migration
medium implementation/high current risk

## Dependencies and Sequencing
- drain or disable old deleter instances during rollout

## Audit Notes
Advisory key is a rolling-deploy protocol: reuse existing writer key so new scrub coordinates with old writers; do not introduce a namespaced/scope-bearing key without staged dual locking.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a deletion scrub and an approved payment-method writer for the same gateway account and subscriber in separate transactions.
2. Observe that deletion hashes scope/account/subscriber while the writer hashes account/subscriber.
3. Confirm both advisory locks can be acquired concurrently and the deletion test reproduces only its own key.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replace self-referential test with canonical writer lock, approved-writer vs scrub contention, 55P03-before-row-change proof, multi-account deterministic order.
- Preserve the exact semantics and compatibility constraints recorded above.

title: [R-41] Give the Jig installer lock an owner and generation
description:
Audit ID: R-41
Authoritative subsystem: INFRA-02
Final rank: 29 of 32
Disposition: recommend
Impact: Removes an ABA race that can permit concurrent install-root mutation and corrupt or destabilize the shared tool installation.
Confidence: high
Estimated effort: medium
Blast radius: medium/generated

## Evidence
- scripts/install-jig.sh:157-161 uses an empty lock directory, 30s wait, fixed 300s stale threshold
- scripts/install-jig.sh:292-303 removes a lock solely by mtime age
- scripts/install-jig.sh:318-330 has no owner/generation/heartbeat
- scripts/install-jig.sh:333-336 unconditional EXIT cleanup removes the path currently at the lock name
- scripts/install-jig.sh:339-355,370-390 holds the lock across cargo install
- scripts/jig:150-162 routes concurrent commands through shared install roots
- .agent/jig-managed-paths.json:19-20 marks installer upstream-template-owned

## Current Complexity
A live install over 300 seconds can have its lock stolen; the old process's trap can then delete the replacement lock (ABA), allowing concurrent writers to one Cargo install root.

## Proposed Representation
Absent | Held { owner_pid, acquisition_id }; atomic mkdir plus owner record, reclaim only a provably dead owner, release only a matching acquisition ID, fail closed on uncertain liveness.

## Smallest Credible Scope
Upstream installer template/rendered snapshot, then regenerate scripts/install-jig.sh; launcher/profile/install-root interfaces unchanged.

## Regression Risk and Migration
Medium: portable PID liveness, reuse, permissions and legacy empty-lock recovery need conservative behavior; retain bounded diagnostics.

## Dependencies and Sequencing
- upstream Jig template change and managed regeneration

## Audit Notes
Coordinator independently verified every cited local line on 2026-08-22.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Keep one Jig cargo install alive for more than 300 seconds.
2. Start a second installer and let it remove the first process's age-stale lock directory and acquire a replacement.
3. Let the first process exit and observe its unconditional trap can remove the replacement lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fake-cargo concurrency harness: live >300s remains exclusive, killed owner reclaim, old exit cannot remove replacement, profile-root reuse unchanged.
